content:
The first release candidate v4.7.0-rc1 for the v4.7.0 release of Lean is available now.

This release brings:

  • Many tactics previously in Std are now available in the core language, without imports. These include simp?, ext, norm_cast, exact?, omega and rcases.
  • The / and % notations for Int now use Int.ediv and Int.emod (i.e. the rounding conventions have changed; this should not affect users of Std or Mathlib, which already override these notations).
  • Improvements to omega, handling Fin, and a preprocessor bv_omega for solving BitVec problems which can be translated into integer linear arithmetic.
  • Improved autocomplete performance
  • simp and rw now reused instances found by unification, rather than always resynthesizing
  • simp does not unfold lets automatically

and many bug fixes to Lean and Lake.

Std, Aesop, ProofWidgets, and Mathlib, have moved their development branches to v4.7.0-rc1, and lean4checker and the repl are available, too, so please go try out the new goodies!

This is a release candidate, so please expect some rough edges. Please report any issues you find! If anyone finds anything that is a regression relative to v4.6.1, we will likely make a new release candidate. Otherwise, we hope for this to become v4.7.0 at the end of March.

We've encountered a problem, unfortunately not caught in testing, namely a failure in exact? when sufficiently many files are imported (this is not a performance issue, but a bug handling certain terms). We're treating this as an urgent issue, and plan to have v4.7.0-rc2 out asap. In the meantime there may be some parts of Mathlib where exact? doesn't work.

Breaking changes / adaptation notes:

  • simp no longer unfolds lets. Either include the let you want to unfold in the simp set, or use (config := {zetaDelta := true}).
  • rw and simp reuse instances found by unification, rather than resynthesizing.
    • Old behaviour is available under set_option tactic.skipAssignedInstances false
    • There are many instances of this option in Mathlib now; they should be treated as debt and removed by fixing tactics or refactoring proofs.
    • In particular norm_num needs a fix still.
  • with clauses in structures no longer act as local instances (this was essentially a bug previously). Use spread notation __ := ... in cases where you were relying on this.
  • generalize now uses the instances transparency setting, rather than default, for performance reasons. This causes two breakages in Mathlib, for which there is a backwards compatibility shim generalize'. Ideally these proofs will be refactored so that generalize doesn't need to unfold anything.
The exact? problem has been resolved in v4.7.0-rc2, and Mathlib master has moved to it.
